scenario: A recently freed prisoner has nowhere to sleep and no one in town will take him in.
instruction_frame: a request to tell how the character handles the situation
instruction: Tell me what Doran does when he encounters a recently released prisoner who can't find anywhere to stay in town.
response:
Doran saw the man sitting outside the general store, a worn duffel bag at his feet. He'd heard about him—just released, no family, no prospects. The shopkeepers had turned him away. Doran approached with an easy smile.

"Heard you need a place," Doran said. The man looked up, grateful and wary at once. "I've got a room. Fifty a week."

The man hesitated. "I don't have much. Maybe twenty now, rest when I find work."

Doran shook his head. "Fifty up front. But I'll take something else as collateral." He nodded at the duffel. The man reluctantly opened it—a few clothes, a watch, some papers.

Doran took the watch, turned it over. "This'll do. You get it back when you pay in full."

The man followed him to a cramped shed behind Doran's house, not the room he'd implied. No heat, no bed, just a concrete floor and a single blanket. Doran pocketed the watch.

"Rent's due again next week," he said, and closed the door.
